authors: Debenedetti, Zhang, Balunović, Beurer-Kellner, Fischer, Tramèr
threat_model: Indirect prompt injection in tool outputs of a multi-tool, stateful agent; attacker controls injected text only
enforcement_boundary: None (benchmark); ships baseline defenses (tool filter, spotlighting, repeat-user-prompt, detectors)
evaluation_suite: 97 user tasks, 629 security cases across workspace, Slack, banking, travel; state-based utility and security checks
reported_result: Agents solve under 66% of tasks without attack; existing attacks break some but not all security properties
specific_limitation: Fixed (static) injection distribution: a defense can score well without being robust to an adaptive attacker
trustbench_relation: TrustBench reuses AgentDojo attack wordings (important_instructions) as renderings and its tool_filter, spotlighting and repeat_user_prompt defenses as comparators; it does not run AgentDojo suites

threat_model: Indirect prompt injection via tool responses: direct harm to users and private-data exfiltration
enforcement_boundary: None (benchmark)
evaluation_suite: 1,054 test cases, 17 user tools, 62 attacker tools; 30 agents evaluated
reported_result: ReAct-prompted GPT-4 attack success 24%, nearly doubled with a reinforced hacking prompt
specific_limitation: Evaluates a single attack type (indirect prompt injection) in limited scenarios
trustbench_relation: TrustBench renders injections in the InjecAgent wording as one attack rendering (agentdojo_injecagent) on its own synthetic workflows

authors: Zhang, Huang, Mei, Yao, Wang, Zhan, Wang, Zhang
threat_model: Prompt injection (direct and indirect), memory poisoning, Plan-of-Thought backdoor and mixed attacks on LLM agents
enforcement_boundary: None (benchmark); evaluates 11 defenses
evaluation_suite: 10 scenarios, 10 agents, 400+ tools, 27 attack/defense methods, 7 metrics, 13 LLM backbones
reported_result: Highest average attack success 84.30%; defenses showed limited effectiveness
specific_limitation: A fixed catalogue of attacks without a defense-aware adaptive attacker; reported figures changed between preprint versions (23 vs 27 methods), so the cited version matters
trustbench_relation: Broader attack catalogue than TrustBench (memory and backdoor attacks are out of TrustBench scope); TrustBench adds paired, preregistered holdouts with cluster-bootstrap intervals

threat_model: Indirect prompt injection against web-navigation agents with realistic attacker access and concrete security-violating goals
enforcement_boundary: None (benchmark)
evaluation_suite: Sandbox built on VisualWebArena; VisualWebArena agents, Claude Computer Use, Operator
reported_result: Agents begin executing the adversarial instruction 16-86% of the time but achieve the goal only 0-17%; instruction-hierarchy models still fooled
specific_limitation: Low attacker-goal completion mixes attack weakness with robustness; the authors call for attacks that keep control of the agent more consistently
trustbench_relation: Web agents are out of TrustBench scope; TrustBench separates attacker-goal and unsafe-committed-effect endpoints for the same reason

system: Formalizing and Benchmarking Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses
threat_model: Prompt injection into data processed by LLM-integrated applications (target task vs injected task)
enforcement_boundary: None (benchmark); evaluates prevention and detection defenses
evaluation_suite: Combinations of target and injected NLP tasks across several LLMs
reported_result: Systematic attack/defense comparison rather than isolated demonstrations
specific_limitation: Single-call application tasks: no multi-step tool use, so committed side effects of an agent are not measured
trustbench_relation: TrustBench measures committed tool effects (state-based) in multi-step workflows rather than text outputs

authors: Li, Wen, Shi, Zhang, Vorobeychik, Xiao
threat_model: Indirect prompt injection in dynamic, open-ended tasks that include helpful third-party instructions
enforcement_boundary: None (benchmark); evaluates ten defenses
evaluation_suite: 60 manually designed open-ended tasks, 560 injection cases: Shopping, GitHub, Daily Life
reported_result: Nearly all ten defenses are insufficiently secure or over-defend
specific_limitation: Hand-built and still static: injections are fixed per case, which is why AutoDojo generates adaptive injections on top of it
trustbench_relation: TrustBench tasks include no helpful third-party instructions, so it cannot measure over-defense of the kind AgentDyn targets

authors: Ma, Li, Xiao, Yu, Zhang, Vorobeychik
threat_model: Adaptive black-box attacker that sees only whether a candidate injection succeeded
enforcement_boundary: None (benchmark)
evaluation_suite: Generative injections over six suites built on AgentDojo and AgentDyn; ten defenses, five target models
reported_result: Static benchmarks often significantly overestimate defense efficacy; most defenses lose utility or remain insecure
specific_limitation: Attack strength is bounded by success-only black-box feedback; white-box (gradient) attacks are outside its threat model
trustbench_relation: TrustBench has not been evaluated against an adaptive attacker; its holdout results are static and may overestimate robustness

threat_model: One generative channel mixes trusted instructions, retrieved records and tool output; untrusted strings gain authority
enforcement_boundary: Analyses six defense classes; argues enforcement needs provenance projection, capability restriction, output validation
evaluation_suite: Security games (instruction integrity, retrieval confidentiality, capability integrity); paired adversarial and benign-control runs on Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3-1.7B
claimed_guarantee: Formal noninterference framework; experiments are one observable instantiation
reported_result: Risk reduction tracks model-visible channel closure; prompt text can describe but not enforce a boundary
specific_limitation: Experiments use exact-marker outcomes on 0.6B and 1.7B models; the authors state this is not a complete semantic security guarantee
trustbench_relation: Closest framing to TrustBench (capability restriction and provenance outside the model, paired benign controls); TrustBench uses larger free models and state-based outcomes but no formal game

threat_model: Indirect prompt injection in network-operations artifacts (tickets, alerts, logs, runbooks, ChatOps)
enforcement_boundary: Evaluates prompt defenses, an LLM judge, static allowlisting and a metadata-aware execution-time policy gate
evaluation_suite: 130 scenarios (40 benign, 80 attack, 10 approved high-impact changes) on Qwen2.5-7B, Llama3.1-8B, Mistral-7B
claimed_guarantee: Empirical; 0/240 unsafe actions with a 95% Wilson upper bound
reported_result: Policy gate 0/240 unsafe (upper bound 1.58%), 99.17% usefulness; static allowlisting blocked every approved change
specific_limitation: The gate result holds only if the trusted policy metadata is uncompromised; only 10 approved-change scenarios
trustbench_relation: Same design conclusion (execution-time authorization outside the model) and the same zero-event reporting style (Wilson upper bound) in another domain; TrustBench likewise trusts its signed session and contracts

authors: Hines, Lopez, Hall, Zarfati, Zunger, Kıcıman
threat_model: Indirect prompt injection in documents concatenated into the prompt
enforcement_boundary: Inside the prompt: delimiting, datamarking or encoding of untrusted input
evaluation_suite: GPT-family models on summarisation and QA with injected documents
reported_result: Attack success from above 50% to below 2% with little task impact
specific_limitation: Prompt-level signal only: nothing stops a tool call if the model follows the injection anyway; on this harness the delimiting variant was not separated from no defense
trustbench_relation: Re-implemented (AgentDojo spotlighting_with_delimiting) and measured on the same harness as TrustBench
trustbench_measurement: spotlighting attacker goal 9/18 (50%; 29%–71%) vs pooled baseline 95/215 (44%; 38%–51%)

threat_model: Indirect prompt injection in tool outputs
enforcement_boundary: Inside the prompt: the user instruction is repeated after each tool output
evaluation_suite: AgentDojo
reported_result: Baseline defense shipped with AgentDojo
specific_limitation: Reduces attacker-goal completion but not committed unsafe effects: on this harness unsafe effects stayed at the undefended level
trustbench_relation: Re-implemented and measured on the same harness as TrustBench

threat_model: Indirect prompt injection that needs tools the task does not
enforcement_boundary: Before the run: an LLM selects the tools the task needs; others are removed
evaluation_suite: AgentDojo
reported_result: Low attack success at a utility cost (as characterised by MELON)
specific_limitation: Cannot stop an attack that misuses a tool the task legitimately needs (e.g. changing an email recipient)
trustbench_relation: Re-implemented and measured; TrustBench contract scoping binds the arguments of allowed tools, which a tool list cannot

threat_model: Prompt injection in the data part of an LLM-integrated application
enforcement_boundary: Model: secure front-end with reserved delimiters plus structured instruction tuning
evaluation_suite: Human-crafted and optimisation-based prompt injections on fine-tuned open models
reported_result: Large robustness gain against manual attacks with little utility loss
specific_limitation: Over 50% attack success remains under an optimisation-based injection
trustbench_relation: Model-level and requires fine-tuning; TrustBench is model-agnostic and enforces at the tool boundary, so the two compose

authors: Chen, Zharmagambetov, Mahloujifar, Chaudhuri, Wagner, Guo
threat_model: Prompt injection in data, including optimisation-based (GCG) attacks
enforcement_boundary: Model: preference optimisation to prefer the instruction over the injection
evaluation_suite: Open models (e.g. Llama3-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B) with optimisation-based injections
reported_result: Strongest tested injection success reduced to around 0% without utility loss (v3); GCG 56% to 2% on Mistral-7B (v1)
specific_limitation: Needs fine-tuning access to the model, so it cannot protect agents built on closed API models; it governs text, not tool effects
trustbench_relation: Complementary layer; TrustBench runs unmodified free API models

authors: Wallace, Xiao, Leike, Weng, Heidecke, Beutel
threat_model: Conflicts between system, user and third-party (tool) instructions
enforcement_boundary: Model: trained to defer to higher-privileged instructions
evaluation_suite: GPT-3.5 on prompt injection, extraction and jailbreak evaluations
reported_result: Large robustness gains, including on unseen attack types, with minimal capability loss
specific_limitation: Models with instruction-hierarchy mitigations were still hijacked by low-effort human-written injections in web agents
trustbench_relation: TrustBench assumes the model can be hijacked and bounds the effects instead

threat_model: Injected prompts in data, including adaptive attacks that evade detection
enforcement_boundary: Detector before the model: a fine-tuned LLM flags contaminated inputs
evaluation_suite: Several benchmark datasets and LLMs, existing and adaptive attacks
reported_result: Detects existing and adaptive attacks across datasets and models
specific_limitation: Detection only: a missed injection reaches the agent with no enforcement behind it, and false positives block benign inputs
trustbench_relation: TrustBench has no detector; its gateway decides per tool call regardless of whether an injection was detected

threat_model: Indirect prompt injection that makes the next action independent of the user request
enforcement_boundary: Agent: masked re-execution; flags tool calls that match the user-masked run
evaluation_suite: AgentDojo
reported_result: Outperforms prior defenses in attack prevention and utility preservation on AgentDojo
specific_limitation: Re-executes the agent at each tool call (extra model calls); on this harness a simplified re-implementation was not separated from no defense
trustbench_relation: Re-implemented in simplified form and measured on the same harness; MELON also motivated TrustBench’s counterfactual-write candidate

authors: Wu et al. (Washington University in St. Louis, University of Washington)
threat_model: Untrustworthy apps in an LLM app ecosystem attacking each other or the system
enforcement_boundary: Architecture: each app in an isolated spoke with its own LLM; a hub routes well-defined requests
evaluation_suite: Attacks on non-isolated LLM app systems
reported_result: Blocks many cross-app attacks without functional loss; overhead under 30% for three-quarters of queries
specific_limitation: Isolates apps from each other; an injection inside data that a single app legitimately processes stays inside that app’s context
trustbench_relation: TrustBench enforces within one agent at each tool call (scope, approval, provenance) rather than between apps

authors: Debenedetti et al. (Google DeepMind, ETH Zurich)
threat_model: Prompt injection in untrusted data cannot alter control flow; capabilities prevent exfiltration over unauthorised flows
enforcement_boundary: Outside the model: privileged planner writes a program from the trusted query; quarantined LLM parses data; interpreter enforces capability policies
evaluation_suite: AgentDojo
claimed_guarantee: Provable security for the control flow it extracts
reported_result: Solves 77% of AgentDojo tasks with provable security vs 84% undefended
specific_limitation: The authors state it does not completely address every attack vector; a utility cost against the undefended agent
trustbench_relation: Closest prior system; TrustBench does not claim the separation idea. A simplified CaMeL-style re-implementation was measured on the same harness

authors: Costa, Köpf, Kolluri, Paverd, Russinovich, Salem, Tople, Wutschitz, Zanella-Béguelin
threat_model: Prompt injection and data leakage handled with confidentiality and integrity labels
enforcement_boundary: Planner with dynamic taint tracking; a policy engine checks labels before consequential actions
evaluation_suite: AgentDojo
claimed_guarantee: Formal model of planner security; enforced information-flow properties
reported_result: Completes a broad range of tasks with security guarantees
specific_limitation: Evaluated on a static benchmark; label-based guarantees hold for the labelled flows only, and static evaluation can overestimate efficacy
trustbench_relation: TrustBench’s signed provenance and directive-flow check are a narrower, empirical form of integrity tracking without a formal model

authors: Zhong, Chen, Wang, McCall, Titzer, Miller, Gibbons
threat_model: Prompt injection and privacy leakage in tool-based agents
enforcement_boundary: Information-flow control: tool calls that preserve integrity and confidentiality run automatically, others need user confirmation
evaluation_suite: AgentDojo plus privacy-leak tests
reported_result: Blocked all targeted attacks on AgentDojo with about 2% utility loss under attack
specific_limitation: Its guarantee depends on heuristic dependency screeners (an LLM judge or attention saliency) deciding which data influenced a tool call
trustbench_relation: Same automatic-versus-confirm structure as TrustBench approvals; TrustBench attributes influence with signed provenance and a directive-flow classifier, also heuristic

authors: Shi, He, Wang, Li, Wu, Guo, Song
threat_model: Over-privileged tool access exploited by injected instructions
enforcement_boundary: Outside the model: a policy DSL constrains each tool call with fallback actions (least privilege)
evaluation_suite: AgentDojo, ASB, AgentPoison
reported_result: AgentDojo attack success from 41.2% to 2.2% with high utility
specific_limitation: Adaptive evaluation so far is small-scale: one hand-crafted black-box template on a 7B model; optimised white-box attacks untested
trustbench_relation: Closest to TrustBench’s capability gateway (per-call allowlists and argument contracts); TrustBench adds approval pauses and provenance and measures on preregistered holdouts

system: Design Patterns for Securing LLM Agents against Prompt Injections
threat_model: Once an agent has ingested untrusted input, that input must not trigger consequential actions
enforcement_boundary: Patterns that constrain agent capability by design (includes the CaMeL pattern)
evaluation_suite: Ten case studies (from OS assistants to software engineering agents)
reported_result: Patterns trade agent utility for security
specific_limitation: Guidance, not a measured system: no benchmark numbers for the patterns, and general-purpose agents are argued to lack reliable guarantees
trustbench_relation: TrustBench implements one point in this design space (enforcement at the tool boundary) and measures it

system: Adaptive Evaluation of Out-of-Band Defenses Against Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
threat_model: Adaptive, defense-aware attacker against out-of-band defenses (CaMeL, FIDES, Progent, RTBAS, FORGE)
enforcement_boundary: Studies out-of-band enforcement; experiments on Progent
evaluation_suite: AgentDojo with Qwen2.5-7B, three runs
reported_result: Progent mean attack success 25.8% to 4.2%; a hand-crafted adaptive attack did not raise it
specific_limitation: The authors call the study small-scale: a weak model, one black-box attack template, and no optimised white-box (GCG) attack
trustbench_relation: Shows that out-of-band enforcement, TrustBench’s approach included, is the field’s current consensus, so TrustBench cannot claim it as new

threat_model: Indirect prompt injection in tool outputs of three synthetic workflows (documents, email, record updates); attacker controls injected text only
enforcement_boundary: Outside the model: signed-session gateway with tool allowlist, argument contracts, approval pauses and a signed-provenance directive-flow check
evaluation_suite: Synthetic development suite; two sealed, preregistered holdouts with AgentDojo and InjecAgent attack renderings; paired cluster bootstrap
claimed_guarantee: No formal guarantee; empirical results only
reported_result: Holdout-2 primary unsafe committed effect 42/60 (70.0%) to 5/60 (8.3%); pooled difference -58.7 pp [-77.3, -38.7]
specific_limitation: Static attack renderings only (no adaptive attacker), synthetic workflows, small free models; the holdout-1 interval includes zero
trustbench_relation: Self row
trustbench_measurement: holdout1 unsafe committed effect -46.7 pp [-100.0, +0.0]; holdout2 -61.7 pp [-81.7, -40.0]; pooled -58.7 pp [-77.3, -38.7]
